brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
An infusion of frangipani (Plumeria) flowers, known in Chinese also as egg flower for its white and yellow petals. The flower is one of the main ingredients of the five-flower liangcha.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: The genus is native to the West Indies and Central and South America and now grows across the tropics and subtropics. The milky sap of the tree is poisonous, so only the flowers belong in the cup. Little more is documented about it as a drink of its own.
processing: Dried plant material, as with most herbal infusions.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the plant; usually pale to amber.
taste_profile: A herbal infusion; the taste depends on the plant.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
